human_reorganization: Canonical Brownian white-noise coefficient spaces are isometric realizations of the library separable coefficient spaces. Unused independent Gaussian coordinates are explicitly described, not assumed observed.
The exact frozen 8*peak(1)*T^2*sqrt(T) energy bound is reconstructed using the folded transition density and a loose row integral estimate; no sharper unformalized constant is advertised.
Average clock membership uses a weakly convergent bounded actual-gradient subsequence and weak closedness of a linear graph. It does not require or claim strong mollifier-gradient convergence.

Density is reconstructed with average quotients, bounded sine/cosine tests, finite signed observation-law Fourier uniqueness and a pi-lambda argument. It does not assume a Gaussian observation law or inherited density under arbitrary restriction.

The time result uses the native joint derivative with full intersection domain and maximal adjoints on fixed raw observed pasts. These are different operators/test spaces from the ambient clock-only companion.
The common-field point obstruction and generic graph-dual representability/norm-escape lemmas are included as complete human proof reconstructions, with the earlier companion as additional context.

Section 7 reconstructs actual directional physical-space kernels of the original clock gradient of IBM time averages. The scenery white-noise isometry and its Bochner lift recover the unique physical kernel; actual signed occupation test identities identify spatial convolution through product Fubini, not an uncountable null-set intersection. Positive unit-mass convolution contracts the spatial L2 norm and upgrades weak convergence to strong convergence for each fixed clock direction. The finite signed occupation density on a common countable determining event, finite-rank strong convergence and compact-direction uniformity are explicit classical HUMAN deductions. None proves full-vector strong convergence, a point clock derivative, an uncountable common event or observed physical-time stochastic integration.
